# Project Context

This project is a **marketing attribution GraphRAG demo** built on Neo4j Aura for an interview. It uses 500 rows of synthetic marketing interaction data to demonstrate graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG).

## Data

**File:** `data/marketing_interactions.csv` — 500 rows, generated by `scripts/generate_marketing_sample.py`

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| `interaction_id` | Unique interaction ID (INT-xxxxx) |
| `occurred_at` | ISO 8601 timestamp |
| `customer_id` | Customer (95 unique) |
| `campaign_id` | Campaign (32 unique) |
| `product_id` | SKU (28 unique) |
| `channel` | paid_search, social_paid, email, webinar, partner, display, organic_social, content_syndication |
| `event_type` | impression, click, landing_view, form_submit, mql, demo_booked, trial_start, purchase |
| `session_id` | Session (grouped interactions) |
| `region` | NA, EMEA, APAC, LATAM |
| `segment` | Enterprise, Mid-Market, SMB, Startup |
| `spend_usd` | Marketing spend |
| `revenue_usd` | Revenue generated (non-zero on purchase/trial/demo events) |
| `creative_id` | Creative asset (45 unique) |
| `agency_id` | Agency (6 unique) |
| `deal_id` | Deal/opportunity (120 unique) |

---

## Neo4j Graph Model

### Nodes

| Label | ID Property | Other Properties |
|---|---|---|
| `Customer` | `customer_id` | `segment`, `region` |
| `Interaction` | `interaction_id` | `occurred_at`, `channel`, `event_type`, `session_id`, `spend_usd`, `revenue_usd`, `embedding` |
| `Campaign` | `campaign_id` | — |
| `Product` | `product_id` | — |
| `Agency` | `agency_id` | — |
| `Creative` | `creative_id` | — |
| `Deal` | `deal_id` | — |
| `Session` | `session_id` | — |

### Relationships

```
(Customer)   -[:HAD_INTERACTION]->  (Interaction)
(Interaction)-[:DURING_CAMPAIGN]->  (Campaign)
(Interaction)-[:FOR_PRODUCT]->      (Product)
(Interaction)-[:VIA_CREATIVE]->     (Creative)
(Campaign)   -[:MANAGED_BY]->       (Agency)
(Customer)   -[:HAS_DEAL]->         (Deal)
(Interaction)-[:LINKED_TO_DEAL]->   (Deal)
(Interaction)-[:IN_SESSION]->       (Session)
```

### Import status

- **783 nodes, 2,666 relationships** imported via Neo4j Aura Data Importer from the CSV
- `Session` nodes were added post-import via Cypher (see below)
- Vector index `interaction_embeddings` created on `Interaction.embedding` (1536 dims, cosine)

---

## Cypher Reference

### Add Session nodes (run once if not already done)
```cypher
MATCH (i:Interaction)
MERGE (s:Session {session_id: i.session_id})
MERGE (i)-[:IN_SESSION]->(s)
```

### Verify schema
```cypher
CALL db.schema.visualization()
```

### Count all nodes by label
```cypher
MATCH (n) RETURN labels(n)[0] AS label, count(n) AS count ORDER BY count DESC
```

### Sample traversal — all products a customer touched
```cypher
MATCH (c:Customer {customer_id: 'CUST-0050'})-[:HAD_INTERACTION]->(i:Interaction)-[:FOR_PRODUCT]->(p:Product)
RETURN c.customer_id, i.event_type, p.product_id
```

### Revenue by agency
```cypher
MATCH (a:Agency)<-[:MANAGED_BY]-(c:Campaign)<-[:DURING_CAMPAIGN]-(i:Interaction)
WHERE i.revenue_usd > 0
RETURN a.agency_id, sum(i.revenue_usd) AS total_revenue ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
```

### Create vector index (run once)
```cypher
CREATE VECTOR INDEX interaction_embeddings IF NOT EXISTS
FOR (i:Interaction) ON (i.embedding)
OPTIONS {indexConfig: {
    `vector.dimensions`: 1536,
    `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine'
}}
```

---

## GraphRAG Stack

| Layer | Tool |
|---|---|
| Graph DB | Neo4j Aura |
| GraphRAG framework | `neo4j-graphrag` (Neo4j's official Python library) |
| Embeddings | OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dims) |
| LLM | OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini` |
| Config | `python-dotenv` via `.env` |

### How GraphRAG works here

1. User question is embedded via `text-embedding-3-small`
2. Neo4j vector index finds the top-K most similar `Interaction` nodes
3. `RETRIEVAL_QUERY` traverses the graph from each matched node to pull in `Customer`, `Campaign`, `Agency`, `Product`, `Deal` context
4. All context is bundled into a prompt sent to `gpt-4o-mini`
5. Answer is returned to the user

The graph traversal in step 3 is what separates GraphRAG from plain vector RAG — it answers relational questions like "which agency" or "which segment" that no single embedded chunk could answer alone.

## Scripts

### `scripts/generate_marketing_sample.py`
Regenerates `data/marketing_interactions.csv`. Seed is fixed at 42 for reproducibility.

### `scripts/embed_interactions.py`
Run **once** after initial import. Generates OpenAI embeddings for all `Interaction` nodes and writes them back to Neo4j. Also creates the vector index.

```bash
python scripts/embed_interactions.py
```

### `scripts/graphrag_app.py`
Interactive GraphRAG app. Type a question or `demo` to run 5 sample questions.

```bash
python scripts/graphrag_app.py
```

---

## Environment Setup

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # fill in your values
pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/embed_interactions.py   # one-time embedding step
python scripts/graphrag_app.py         # start the app
```

**`.env` keys:**
```
NEO4J_URI=neo4j+s://<your-aura-id>.databases.neo4j.io
NEO4J_USER=neo4j
NEO4J_PASSWORD=<your-password>
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
```

## Cost Estimate (OpenAI)

| Operation | Est. cost |
|---|---|
| Embed 500 interactions (one-time) | ~$0.0001 |
| Per question (embed + GPT-4o-mini) | ~$0.001–$0.003 |
| 100 demo questions | ~$0.10–$0.30 |

$5 OpenAI credit will last a very long time for demo purposes.

## Interview Talking Points

- **Why graph over pure vector RAG:** A flat embedded chunk has no awareness of relationships. The graph lets the retriever walk from an `Interaction` to its `Agency`, `Customer segment`, `Deal`, etc. in one traversal — richer context = better answers.
- **Three retriever types in `neo4j-graphrag`:**
  - `VectorRetriever` — pure semantic search, no graph traversal
  - `VectorCypherRetriever` — semantic search + graph traversal (used here)
  - `Text2CypherRetriever` — LLM converts NL question to Cypher, good for analytical/aggregation queries
- **MERGE vs CREATE on import:** Using `MERGE` on node IDs during import deduplicates automatically — 500 CSV rows with 95 unique customers become 95 `Customer` nodes, not 500.
- **Vector index dimensions must match the embedding model:** `text-embedding-3-small` = 1536 dims. Changing models requires dropping and recreating the index and re-embedding.
